claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr and MoNbTaW are examples of body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloys.
The target alloy is a disordered single-phase bcc solid solution at high temperature and lacks long-range order.
Bcc refractory high-entropy alloys can have a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range ordering.
Controlled annealing or thermal cycling can evolve SRO from isolated clusters into a percolating network while avoiding phase decomposition.
The relevant operating regime is above 0.5 Tm while the alloy remains single-phase bcc.
Standard interatomic potentials fail to capture the correct SRO energetics or evolution in the target refractory alloy.
Accurate modeling of SRO in the target system requires a machine-learning potential or a highly accurate first-principles description.
SRO clusters can form a connected network spanning the grain volume.
A spanning SRO network alters phonon dispersion and provides a pathway with lower scattering cross-sections than the disordered matrix.
Isolated SRO clusters behave as point defects that increase phonon scattering and reduce thermal conductivity.
Percolation of SRO clusters creates a continuous ordered region in which local lattice periodicity is restored.
Restored local periodicity reduces Umklapp and phonon-defect scattering and increases phonon mean free path.
Thermal conductivity undergoes a non-monotonic transition and increases when SRO connectivity crosses a percolation threshold.
The conductivity enhancement exceeds linear, series/parallel, or effective-medium mixing-model predictions and scales with SRO-network connectivity.
Non-percolating SRO regimes and fcc systems exhibit a scattering-dominated reduction in thermal conductivity.
Composition changes or annealing can cause high-entropy alloys to decompose into multiple phases.
AlCoCrFeNi-related alloys can exhibit single B2 or two-phase BCC plus B2 microstructures.

Macroscopic phase separation or intermetallic precipitation shifts transport control to grain-boundary scattering and interface resistance, invalidating the proposed percolative enhancement mechanism.
SRO enhances edge-dislocation mobility but reduces the rate of double-kink nucleation for screw dislocations in bcc MoNbTaW.
The predicted percolation threshold and conductivity enhancement depend critically on accurate prediction of SRO cluster size and connectivity by the potential-energy model.
